scenes.text: [whispers] Okay... see this code? It shipped three sprints ago. And it has never run. Not once. [laughs] Can you spot why?
One typo... and every Flagsmith SDK just quietly says: off. [sighs] Because your flags live in a dashboard, five clicks away from your code. [sarcastic] Super fun at two A.M.
So I built FlagLens. [excited] Your Flagsmith flags, live, right inside VS Code. Made for self-hosted, open-source Flagsmith.
Two commands. Make up, make seed... and real Flagsmith is running in Docker, with a demo project. [laughs softly] Zero clicking.
Open the project, click connect, and boom: every flag lights up with its live state, in every environment.
Flip one. Confirm. The shop changes on the very next request. No redeploy.
Production, though? [laughs] Nope. You type the flag's name first. And yes, there's an undo.
Okay, my favourite part. FlagLens greys out code that can't run in the environment you're looking at. Switch to Production, and it updates. Hmm... and it only greys what's certain. No false alarms.

But users aren't all the same. [curious] So what does Alice, our beta tester, actually get? FlagLens runs Flagsmith's own rules, locally: her segment, her bucket, her values. And it matches the real server. Fourteen thousand checks... zero misses.
It even checks your targeting rules. This EU override? It never fires. Pro plan grabs those users first. And this UK one... [laughs] changes absolutely nothing.
Testing six flags together? That's ninety-six combinations. [sighs] Or... seven runs that cover every pair. Provably the minimum. [laughs softly] Thanks, maths.
Plus drift between staging and production, one-click typo fixes, stale flags... [excited] all free, on open source.
FlagLens. Clone it, make up, make seed, and you're live in five minutes. [laughs softly] Your future self will thank you.
